outcome: Help journalists retrieve, compare and cite trusted evidence faster while preserving editorial independence, source protection and human publication authority.
overview: Newsrooms work against fast cycles with evidence scattered across licensed databases, their own archive and the open web, so research takes longer than the story allows and context is missed. This solution retrieves and compares evidence from sources the newsroom has approved, returns every statement with a citation, date and permission status, and highlights contradictions between sources instead of resolving them. Nothing is published automatically: journalists and editors keep full authority over what is true, what is printed and what is corrected. A 6–10 week desk pilot targets faster verified research, with source protection and editorial independence treated as design constraints.

benefits.text: Reduce source-discovery and verification time by a target 30% on the pilot desk
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Target from the source catalogue, to validate against the desk’s own research-time baseline during the pilot — not a guarantee

benefits.text: Give every statement in a research brief a citation, a date and a permission status
benefits.source: Architecture design — retrieval returns cited passages only, and uncited assertions are withheld
benefits.limits: Citations show where a statement came from, not that the source is right; editorial verification remains a human judgement

benefits.text: Surface contradictions and stale evidence across approved sources for the journalist to weigh
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Contradiction detection is assistive and incomplete; it never adjudicates which source is correct

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (e.g. UAE, KSA); archive content, research sessions and source material remain in the customer tenancy in the reference designs, with confidential-source material isolated from model training and vendor telemetry

notFor.situation: There is no editorial or source policy defining what counts as an approved source
notFor.why: The system retrieves only from sources the newsroom has approved; without that list it would rank the open web, which is precisely the failure mode being addressed

notFor.situation: Autonomous publication or automated fact verdicts are the goal
notFor.why: Determining truth and deciding to publish are editorial acts with legal and ethical consequence; the design deliberately has no path to publish without a named editor

notFor.situation: Confidential-source material would need to pass through the same pipeline
notFor.why: Source protection cannot be delegated to a retrieval system; material identifying a confidential source must remain outside the indexed corpus

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the customer owns editorial standards, source approval, publication and corrections — none of which the platform decides · Duration: 6–10 week pilot; further 12–22 weeks to newsroom-wide rollout
Delivery pod: Partner delivery lead + project manager, retrieval engineer, data engineer; customer editorial standards owner, research editor, legal reviewer, information-security approver · Support model: Business-hours or 24×7 option; severity-based response targets; partner service desk with vendor escalation
1) Discovery and research-time baseline agreement
2) Source approval, licence mapping and corpus onboarding
3) Retrieval and evidence-workspace build
4) Gold-question evaluation and adversarial-source red teaming
5) Editorial UAT, training and controlled desk rollout
6) Stabilisation and handover
deliverables: Gold-question set meets the agreed citation, date and permission accuracy thresholds
Adversarial and manipulated sources are handled without instruction-following or unattributed assertion
Source-protection controls verified, including log retention and export restrictions
The CMS boundary is one-way and requires named editor approval
Editorial UAT complete with the standards editor signed off
effort: 6–10 week pilot; further 12–22 weeks to newsroom-wide rollout
languages: Arabic and English retrieval, cross-language comparison and cited drafting; delivery in English with Arabic editorial review support
